headline: Four megacaps dragged the S&P up 0.5% while equal-weight/cap-weight printed a 52-week low and crude reversed +2.3% — yesterday's two reliefs are down to one.
summary: Yesterday the tape offered two reliefs: energy cracking and the front end blinking. One of them was withdrawn today. WTI reversed +2.3% to 91.41 (+33.3% on the quarter, +59.2% YTD), oil/gold +2.0% to a 79th-percentile reading and +14.0% on the month with acceleration 1.18, and DBC +1.4%. Breakevens still refuse to move — 5y 2.34%, 10y 2.35%, both roughly flat for a week — so this is not an inflation-expectations story, it is the term-premium engine getting its fuel back. The rates picture itself was static (10y 5.26%, 30y 5.59%, both at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks; 2y 4.89%; 10y real yield 2.91%, +49bp on the month with acceleration 1.42), but the volatility leg kept grinding: MOVE +1.0% to 107.65, +42.9% on the month, z=2.34, acceleration 1.84. TLT, IEF and LQD are all still sitting at the 0th percentile of their 52-week ranges. Rates composite -83, risk regime unchanged at -19.

The index lied louder today than yesterday. SPX +0.5% to 7,708.7 and NDX +0.8% were bought by four names — GOOGL +3.0%, AAPL +2.2%, AMZN +1.8%, MSFT +1.7% — with QQQ/SPY z=1.33 and rising. Equal weight went the other way, -0.1%, and RSP/SPY fell another 0.6% to the 3rd percentile of the last year with z=-2.18 and acceleration -1.36. That is a fresh relative low, not a base. IWM/SPY is -5.1% on the month, IYT/SPY sits at the 1st percentile, XHB/SPY at the 0.5th, XRT/SPY at the 1.3rd. The consumer block inside that is genuinely broken: HD -12.2% on the month at the 0th percentile, MCD -10.8% with z=-2.32 also at the 0th, NKE at the 0.3rd, WMT -1.2% today, XLY -6.1% on the month with relative strength -6.5%. With the 30-year mortgage at 7.03% (+38bp on the month, 100th percentile), ITB -6.9% and DHI -4.6% are the transmission mechanism working exactly as designed.

Two things I flagged yesterday resolved badly. First, the precious-metals repair failed its third test: gold was up 0.3% but GDX -0.9%, GDXJ -1.0%, NEM -0.7%, and GDX/gold slipped 0.4% with acceleration -2.72. Miners refusing to follow bullion higher after a -6.5% month in gold is a de-rate, not a bottom. Second, the hard-asset and power complex is still in outright liquidation: CEG -4.2% today (-7.8% on the month, 10th percentile), VST -1.8%, NLR -11.7% on the month at the 3rd percentile, URA -11.6%, REMX -16.7% with acceleration -1.95, XME -11.2%. Financials remain the cleanest ongoing damage — XLF -0.6% today and -6.7% on the month with relative strength -7.0% despite 3m10y at 1.01 and the 100th percentile of steepness. BX -1.3% to -21.5% on the month (z=-2.19, acceleration -2.12), GS -11.3%, IAI -8.6%, KBE -0.8%. Curve steepening is not saving these; capital-markets and private-credit marks are the story.

The offsets are real but narrow. Credit still hasn't paid for any of this: HYG flat on the day with HYG/IEF at the 97.6th percentile, BKLN unchanged, VIX 15.91 at the 14th percentile and VIX3M at the 6th, credit/vol composite +23. Growth pulse is +14 with copper +1.2% and copper/gold at the 96.5th percentile, acceleration 1.36 — no demand recession is being priced. Crypto quietly turned: BTC +7.3% on the month, ETH +9.1%, SOL +16.7%, MSTR +16.3%, all four in turning_up, and BTC only at the 39th percentile of the last year. Brazil is the one EM working — BVSP +1.5%, EWZ +2.0% — against a dollar squeeze that has rotated into LatAm and Asia: USDMXN +0.6% to 18.083 with z=2.38 and acceleration 1.97, USDBRL +0.7%, AUDJPY -1.0% with z=-1.85, EWY -2.1%, EWT -1.0%, TUR -2.2% and -15.8% on the month. The asymmetry is clear: vol is priced at the 14th percentile of the year while breadth is at the 3rd and bond vol at z=2.34.

good.text: Crude turned back up and the cyclical metals confirmed it — WTI +2.3% to 91.41, copper +1.2%, copper/gold at the 96.5th percentile with acceleration 1.36, growth pulse +14. Nothing here is pricing a demand collapse.
Megacap tech is not just holding, it is broadening within itself: GOOGL +3.0%, AAPL +2.2%, AMZN +1.8%, MSFT +1.7%, plus IGV +1.7% and CIBR +1.9%. SMH is +9.3% on the month, MU +11.9%, AMD +28.3%.
Credit has still absorbed none of the duration damage. HYG flat on the day, HYG/IEF at the 97.6th percentile and up 0.9% on the month, BKLN unchanged, credit/vol composite +23.
The front end is still leaning toward cuts: 3-month 4.25% and 2-year 4.89%, both -3bp, with 3m10y at 1.01 and the 100th percentile of its range. The easing option has not been taken off the table.
Crypto flipped to turning_up across the complex — BTC +7.3% on the month and +40.5% on the quarter, ETH +9.1%, SOL +16.7%, MSTR +16.3% — from only the 39th percentile of the 52-week range.
Brazil and peripheral Europe are the surviving non-US longs: BVSP +1.5%, EWZ +2.0% (+3.2% on the month), GREK +1.1% and +4.0% on the week, EPOL +15.1% on the quarter.

bad.text: Breadth made a new low, not a base. RSP/SPY -0.6% to the 3rd percentile with z=-2.18 and acceleration -1.36; IWM/SPY -5.1% on the month; equal weight -4.3% while SPX is +0.3%. This is an accelerating narrowing, which is the bad kind of acceleration.

Bond volatility keeps compounding with no buyer: MOVE 107.65, +42.9% on the month, z=2.34, acceleration 1.84, while the 10-year real yield sits at 2.91% (+49bp, acceleration 1.42) and TLT, IEF and LQD are all at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks.

Oil's reversal reloads the term-premium trade that energy weakness had just started to defuse — WTI +2.3%, oil/gold +14.0% on the month at the 79th percentile, DBC +1.4% — with breakevens inert at 2.35%. Inflation composite -33.

Financials are bleeding through a steepening curve, which means it is marks, not margin: XLF -6.7% on the month with relative strength -7.0%, BX -21.5% (acceleration -2.12), GS -11.3%, IAI -8.6%, KBE -6.1%.

The consumer is the weakest block in the market. HD -12.2% on the month at the 0th percentile, MCD -10.8% with z=-2.32 also at the 0th, NKE at the 0.3rd, XLY -6.1%, XRT/SPY at the 1.3rd percentile. Mortgage rates at 7.03% are pushing ITB -6.9% and XHB/SPY to the 0.5th percentile.

The gold-miner bounce failed on the third day and the hard-asset/power complex is still liquidating: GDX -0.9% and GDXJ -1.0% against gold +0.3%, GDX/gold acceleration -2.72, NEM acceleration -2.75; CEG -4.2%, NLR -11.7% on the month at the 3rd percentile, REMX -16.7%, XME -11.2%.

trades.name: Short the long end / 2s30s steepener
trades.line: Short duration: TLT puts + pay 30s vs receive 2s
trades.expr: Buy TLT Dec 75 puts, partially financed by selling the Dec 82 calls; institutionally, duration-neutral 2s30s steepener — short Ultra Bond (UB) futures against long 2-yr (ZT).
trades.thesis: This is a term-premium event, not an inflation event: 10y real yield 2.91% (+49bp on the month, acceleration 1.42) against 10y breakevens pinned at 2.35%. The long end has no bid and the volatility that would force convexity hedging is still rising.
trades.trigger: 30y 5.59% and 10y 5.26% both at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks; MOVE +42.9% on the month to 107.65 with z=2.34 and acceleration 1.84; TLT, IEF and LQD all at the 0th percentile; and crude reversing +2.3% today removes the disinflation excuse that briefly capped the long end.
trades.stop: TLT closes above 81, or 30y trades back under 5.35%, or MOVE breaks below 95 — any of which says the vol spiral is over.

trades.name: Long QQQ vs short IWM
trades.line: Long QQQ / short IWM: breadth is dying, not repairing
trades.expr: $10m long QQQ against $8.5m short IWM (beta-matched); roll monthly.
trades.thesis: With the 2-year at 4.89% and real yields at 2.91%, the small and mid-cap complex cannot fund its way out. Liquidity is concentrating into a handful of cash-generative megacaps, and that concentration is accelerating, not mean-reverting.
trades.trigger: RSP/SPY -0.6% to the 3rd percentile of 52 weeks (z=-2.18, acceleration -1.36) and IWM/SPY -5.1% on the month, while QQQ rose 0.8% on GOOGL +3.0%, AAPL +2.2%, MSFT +1.7% and QQQ/SPY z=1.33.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY reclaims its 200-day (currently 4.5% above spot), or the spread loses 4%. A 2-year break below 4.60% would also revive the laggards — cut it.

trades.name: Short financials / capital markets
trades.line: Short XLF: curve steepened, banks fell anyway
trades.expr: Short XLF outright, or buy Nov 52 puts; purer version is a short basket of BX/GS/IAI against a long SPY hedge.
trades.thesis: If a 3m10y curve at the 100th percentile cannot lift bank stocks, the problem is asset marks, not net interest margin. Private-credit and capital-markets exposure is repricing in equity before it shows in spreads — and HYG/IEF at the 97.6th percentile means the credit market hasn't started.
trades.trigger: XLF -0.6% today, -6.7% on the month with relative strength -7.0% and z=-1.58; BX -21.5% on the month with z=-2.19 and acceleration -2.12; GS -11.3%; IAI -8.6%; KRE and KBE both rolling over.
trades.stop: XLF reclaims 56, or BX closes above 125 and holds a week.

trades.name: Long XOP vs short OIH
trades.line: Long XOP / short OIH: crude up, service capex broken
trades.thesis: Crude is trading its own supply story, not a demand collapse — copper is up and copper/gold is at the 96.5th percentile. E&Ps monetise the barrel directly; oil service is the levered capex bet and it is being liquidated even as the commodity rallies.
trades.trigger: WTI +2.3% to 91.41 (+33.3% on the quarter) with XOP +1.7% today and 3-month relative strength +14.8%, against OIH -11.5% on the month with acceleration -1.36 and relative strength -11.8%.
trades.stop: WTI closes below 85, or OIH outperforms XOP by 4% on the pair.

trades.name: Long USD/MXN
trades.line: Long USDMXN: the squeeze has rotated into LatAm carry
trades.expr: Buy 3-month USD/MXN 18.25/19.00 call spread; equity proxy is a short in EWW.
trades.thesis: With US 2-year yields at 4.89% and the dollar turning up, the highest-carry EM currencies are where the unwind concentrates. Mexico is the crowded carry leg and it is breaking first.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +0.6% to 18.083, +4.6% on the week and +6.2% on the month, z=2.38 with acceleration 1.97 — the most extreme z-score in the entire FX block; USDBRL +0.7%; EWW -1.1% today and -7.1% on the month; DXY turning up with acceleration 0.90.
trades.stop: USDMXN back below 17.60, or DXY breaks 100.

trades.name: Long index tail hedge
trades.line: Buy the hedge: VIX is at the 14th pctile, MOVE at z=2.34
trades.expr: Buy Dec SPX 7300/6800 put spread, partly financed by selling the Dec 8100 call; or VIX Nov 20/30 call spread for a smaller premium outlay.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced as if breadth were fine. It isn't. Cross-asset vol divergence this wide — bond vol at z=2.34, VIX3M at the 6th percentile — has historically closed via equity, not via bonds calming down.
trades.trigger: VIX 15.91 at the 14th percentile and VIX3M at the 6th, SKEW -3.5% on the month making wings cheap, while RSP/SPY prints a 3rd-percentile low and MOVE is +42.9% on the month. VIX/VIX3M has turned up to 0.879.
trades.stop: Premium-capped. Cut if SPX holds above 7,900 with RSP/SPY reclaiming its 200-day.

trades.name: Long bitcoin via IBIT
trades.line: Long IBIT: whole complex flipped to turning_up, still cheap
trades.expr: Long IBIT, sized small (1-2% NAV), add on a hold above the 200-day.
trades.thesis: Bitcoin is the one risk asset that has already had its bear market — down 26.1% over a year — and is now re-accelerating off a low base while everything else is extended. It is the cleanest expression of any front-end easing that the 3-month and 2-year are hinting at.
trades.trigger: BTC +7.3% on the month and +40.5% on the quarter to 84,322, ETH +9.1%, SOL +16.7%, MSTR +16.3% — all four in turning_up — with BTC still only at the 39th percentile of its 52-week range and relative strength to the S&P +7.0% on the month.
trades.stop: BTC closes below 76,000 (roughly the 200-day, currently 14.1% below spot). COIN -5.2% on the week is the live divergence to watch — it is why this is size-1.
